summary: The parallel (longitudinal) dissipative force in pair dpd/ext/tstat/kk has the wrong sign - the leading minus of the CPU expression is missing, turning the drag term into an energy-pumping anti-drag.
failure_scenario: Any run with `pair_style dpd/ext/tstat` under `-sf kk`: the longitudinal friction becomes negative friction, so relative radial velocities are amplified instead of damped every step; the thermostat no longer holds the target temperature and the system heats up and typically blows up (lost atoms), while the pure-CPU style is stable.
suggested_fix: Change line 302 to `fpair = -params(itype,jtype).gamma*wdPar*wdPar*dot*rinv;` (keeping the following `fpair *= factor_dpd;`).

summary: During a temperature ramp (t_start != t_stop) pair dpd/ext/tstat/kk updates only the parallel noise amplitude sigma and never the perpendicular one sigmaT, so the transverse random force stays at the initial temperature.
failure_scenario: `pair_style dpd/ext/tstat 1.0 5.0 <cut> <seed>` under -sf kk: the transverse dissipation grows with the ramped gammaT-based drag while the transverse noise amplitude stays at T=1.0, breaking the fluctuation-dissipation balance; the perpendicular degrees of freedom equilibrate to the wrong (starting) temperature.
suggested_fix: Also set `k_params.view_host()(i,j).sigmaT = k_params.view_host()(j,i).sigmaT = sqrt(2.0*boltz*temperature*gammaT[i][j]);` inside the same loop.

summary: Sign error in the parallel dissipative force: KOKKOS has fpair = gamma*wdPar^2*dot*rinv (then *= factor_dpd), the CPU style has fpair = -factor_dpd*gamma*wdPar^2*dot*rinv. The drag term becomes an anti-drag that pumps energy into the system.
verified_by: orchestrator (read src/KOKKOS/pair_dpd_ext_tstat_kokkos.cpp:301-303 vs src/DPD-BASIC/pair_dpd_ext_tstat.cpp:147). Note the sibling pair_dpd_ext_kokkos.cpp:301 uses 'fpair -= ...' which is correct there because a conservative term was accumulated first; the tstat variant has no conservative term so it needs the explicit minus.

summary: Temperature-ramp block updates only params.sigma; the CPU style updates sigma AND sigmaT. The perpendicular random force stays at the initial temperature for the whole ramp.
FixWallFlowKokkos::init() replaces the base init() instead of calling it, silently dropping the triclinic, rigid-body and box-change compatibility checks that FixWallFlow::init() performs.
evidence: fix_wall_flow_kokkos.cpp:57-68 'template <class DeviceType> void FixWallFlowKokkos<DeviceType>::init() { atomKK->sync(execution_space, datamask_read); k_current_segment.template sync<DeviceType>(); d_x = ...; copymode = 1; Kokkos::parallel_for(...TagFixWallFlowInit...); copymode = 0; k_current_segment.template modify<DeviceType>(); }' - there is no 'FixWallFlow::init();' call.  The base version (src/fix_wall_flow.cpp:185-217) does much more than fill current_segment: 'if (domain->triclinic != 0) error->all(FLERR, "Fix wall/flow cannot be used with triclinic simulation box");' plus the loop over modify->get_fix_list() that raises 'Fix wall/flow is not compatible with rigid bodies' (nrigid) and 'Fix wall/flow is not compatible with simulation box size changing along flow direction' (box_change on the flow axis).  Only the last five lines of that function (the current_segment fill) are reproduced by the kernel.  Every other /kk style in this group calls its base init() first (e.g. fix_viscous_kokkos.cpp:112, fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:80, fix_ti_spring_kokkos.cpp:76).
failure_scenario: 'fix wall/flow/kk x ...' combined with 'fix rigid' or with 'fix npt' straining the flow axis, or a 'change_box ... triclinic' issued after the fix was defined: the plain CPU fix stops with a clear error, the /kk variant runs and produces wrong results (the wall coordinates walls.front()/back() were frozen at construction from domain->boxlo/boxhi, so a changing box silently misplaces the walls).
suggested_fix: Call FixWallFlow::init() at the top of FixWallFlowKokkos::init() (its current_segment loop is harmless and is immediately overwritten by the device kernel), or replicate the three checks.

summary: datamask_read omits V_MASK although end_of_step's kernel writes only selected entries of the velocity array and then claims the whole array as device-modified, so a host-side velocity update made earlier in the step is discarded.
evidence: fix_wall_flow_kokkos.cpp:38-39 'datamask_read = X_MASK | RMASS_MASK | TYPE_MASK | MASK_MASK; datamask_modify = V_MASK;'.  end_of_step (fix_wall_flow_kokkos.cpp:81-101) only does 'atomKK->sync(execution_space, datamask_read);' and then binds 'd_v = atomKK->k_v.template view<DeviceType>();' (:85); the kernel writes just three components for the atoms that crossed a wall (fix_wall_flow_kokkos.cpp:156-160 'd_v(atom_i, flowax) = v * direction; ...') and the call ends with 'atomKK->modified(execution_space, datamask_modify);' (:101).  src/KOKKOS/modify_kokkos.cpp wraps every fix callback with exactly the same pair ('atomKK->sync(fix[i]->execution_space,fix[i]->datamask_read); ... atomKK->modified(fix[i]->execution_space,fix[i]->datamask_modify);'), so nothing else brings v to the device.  Sibling styles that partially overwrite v do sync it first, e.g. fix_temp_berendsen_kokkos.cpp:145 'atomKK->sync(execution_space,V_MASK|MASK_MASK);' and fix_temp_csld_kokkos.cpp:162.
failure_scenario: any run mixing 'fix wall/flow/kk' with a non-KOKKOS style that writes velocities on the host (a plain 'fix langevin', 'fix momentum', or the exchange_comm_legacy Domain::pbc path, src/KOKKOS/domain_kokkos.cpp:381 'atomKK->modified(Host,X_MASK|V_MASK|MASK_MASK|IMAGE_MASK)'): the device copy of v is never refreshed, the fix marks it as the newest version, and every velocity except those of the few wall-crossing atoms silently reverts to an older state.
suggested_fix: Add V_MASK to datamask_read in the constructor (or call 'atomKK->sync(execution_space, V_MASK)' in end_of_step before binding d_v).

summary: unpack_exchange_kokkos writes d_current_segment on the device and marks it device-modified without first syncing it there, so a pending host-side modification of current_segment is dropped for the atoms the kernel does not touch.
evidence: fix_wall_flow_kokkos.cpp:279-295: the function binds d_buf/d_indices, launches TagFixWallFlowUnpackExchange (which writes 'd_current_segment(index) = ...' for received atoms only, :276) and ends with 'k_current_segment.template modify<DeviceType>();' - there is no 'k_current_segment.template sync<DeviceType>();'.  Its own pack_exchange_kokkos does perform that sync (fix_wall_flow_kokkos.cpp:237), and both sibling styles built from the same template sync before the unpack kernel: fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:286 'k_xoriginal.template sync<DeviceType>();' and fix_ti_spring_kokkos.cpp:277.  The host side can legitimately be the newer one, because copy_arrays (:187-192) and unpack_exchange (:262-268) both end with k_current_segment.modify_host().
failure_scenario: a legacy host sort (AtomKokkos::sort() falls back to it when any other extra-grow fix lacks sort_device) marks current_segment host-modified via copy_arrays; on the next device exchange in which this rank sends no atoms for a dimension but receives some, pack_exchange_kokkos is skipped (comm_kokkos.cpp:1369 'if (nsend) { ... }') so no sync happens, and unpack_exchange_kokkos then promotes the stale device copy - atoms get the wrong segment and are re-thermostatted spuriously (or not at all) at the next wall crossing.
suggested_fix: Add 'k_current_segment.template sync<DeviceType>();' before the parallel_for in unpack_exchange_kokkos, matching pack_exchange_kokkos and the sibling styles.

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly); found by rules_C
summary: datamask_read omits V_MASK while the kernel partially overwrites v and datamask_modify claims V_MASK, so the device velocity array is claimed authoritative without ever being synced from a host-side writer.
evidence: fix_wall_flow_kokkos.cpp:38-39, 81 (sync datamask_read only), 101 (modified V_MASK).
failure_scenario: GPU run where v was last written on the host (velocity command, non-kk fix, host exchange): after end_of_step every non-crossing atom's velocity silently reverts to a stale device copy.
suggested_fix: Add V_MASK to datamask_read.

summary: fix wall/flow/kk lists V_MASK only in datamask_modify, never in datamask_read, so the device copy of v is never synced before the kernel partially overwrites it.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_flow_kokkos.cpp:38-39 `datamask_read = X_MASK | RMASS_MASK | TYPE_MASK | MASK_MASK;` / `datamask_modify = V_MASK;`.  end_of_step() at line 81 does only `atomKK->sync(execution_space, datamask_read);` (no V_MASK), then line 85 `d_v = atomKK->k_v.template view<DeviceType>();` and the kernel writes it in generate_velocity_kk() lines 156-160 (`d_v(atom_i, flowax) = ...`, `d_v(atom_i,(flowax+1)%3) = ...`, `d_v(atom_i,(flowax+2)%3) = ...`) for the subset of atoms that crossed a wall, and finally line 101 `atomKK->modified(execution_space, datamask_modify);` marks the whole device v newer than host.
failure_scenario: GPU run where v was last written on the host (a non-KOKKOS fix/compute, `velocity` command, or a host-side exchange/borders which does atomKK->modified(Host, datamask_exchange) including V_MASK in comm_kokkos.cpp:1043/1483): end_of_step syncs only x/rmass/type/mask to the device, the kernel rewrites v only for wall-crossing atoms in the stale device buffer, then modified(Device,V_MASK) makes that stale buffer authoritative -- every other atom's velocity silently reverts to an older value.
suggested_fix: Add V_MASK to datamask_read in the constructor (line 38), i.e. `datamask_read = X_MASK | V_MASK | RMASS_MASK | TYPE_MASK | MASK_MASK;`.

summary: ~FixPropertyAtomKokkos() calls atomKK->update_property_atom() while the dying fix is still in Modify's fix list, so AtomKokkos::fix_prop_atom[] is rebuilt containing a pointer to the object being destroyed (use-after-free on every later atomKK->sync()/modified()).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_property_atom_kokkos.cpp:63-85: 'FixPropertyAtomKokkos::~FixPropertyAtomKokkos() { ... atomKK->update_property_atom(); }'. src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp:162-180: 'void AtomKokkos::update_property_atom() { nprop_atom = 0; ... for (auto &ifix : modify->get_fix_by_style("^property/atom")) { ... ++nprop_atom; prop_atom_fixes.push_back(ifix); } ... fix_prop_atom[n++] = dynamic_cast<FixPropertyAtomKokkos *>(ifix); }'. src/modify.cpp Modify::delete_fix(int ifix): 'delete fix[ifix]; atom->update_callback(ifix); for (int i = ifix + 1; i < nfix; i++) fix[i - 1] = fix[i]; ... nfix--;' -- the entry is removed from fix[] only AFTER the destructor has run, and src/modify.cpp Modify::get_fix_by_style() iterates 'for (int ifix = 0; ifix < nfix; ifix++) if (fix[ifix] && utils::strmatch(fix[ifix]->style, style))', so the fix currently being destroyed still matches. AtomKokkos::sync()/modified() then dereference it: src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp 'for (int n = 0; n < nprop_atom; n++) fix_prop_atom[n]->sync(space, mask);'.
failure_scenario: fix p all property/atom d_foo ; run 100 ; unfix p ; run 100  -> the first atomKK->sync() in the second run calls sync()/modified() on the freed FixPropertyAtomKokkos object (heap use-after-free: crash, or silent corruption of the DualView modify flags).
suggested_fix: Do not rebuild the list from inside the destructor; instead have AtomKokkos::update_property_atom() skip the fix being destroyed (pass 'this' to exclude), or trigger the rebuild from Modify::delete_fix()/Atom::update_callback() after the fix has been removed from modify->fix[].

summary: Nothing forces 'fix property/atom' to the /kk variant under KOKKOS, yet AtomKokkos::add_custom() always allocates the custom arrays as Kokkos views; the non-kk FixPropertyAtom::grow_arrays() then calls memory->grow()/realloc() on a pointer that aliases into a Kokkos allocation.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp:466-477 (AtomKokkos::add_custom, flag==1 && cols==0): 'dvector = (double **) memory->srealloc(...); this->sync(Device, DVECTOR_MASK); memoryKK->grow_kokkos(k_dvector, dvector, ndvector, nmax, "atom:dvector"); ...' and src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h grow_kokkos() sets 'array[i] = &data.view_host()(i,0)'. src/fix_property_atom.cpp FixPropertyAtom::grow_arrays() then does 'memory->grow(atom->dvector[index[nv]], nmax, "atom:dvector"); memset(&atom->dvector[index[nv]][nmax_old], 0, nbytes);' -- Memory::grow() calls srealloc()/realloc() on that Kokkos-owned pointer. The only guard, src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp:162-170 AtomKokkos::update_property_atom() ('if (!ifix->kokkosable) error->all(FLERR, "KOKKOS package requires a Kokkos-enabled version of fix property/atom")'), is reached only from FixPropertyAtomKokkos's own constructor/destructor, so it never runs when every property/atom fix in the run is non-kk. src/lammps.cpp:465 shows suffix_enable is set only by -sf/-suffix, and src/modify.h:108 add_fix() applies the suffix only when suffix_enable is set.
failure_scenario: lmp -k on t 4 -in in.reaxff (no -sf kk) with 'pair_style reaxff/kk' and 'fix 1 all reaxff/species/kk ...': FixReaxFFSpecies::setup() runs modify->add_fix("clusterID_... all property/atom d_... ghost yes"), which resolves to the plain FixPropertyAtom; its post_constructor()->grow_arrays(atom->nmax) reallocs a Kokkos pointer -> glibc 'realloc(): invalid pointer' abort or silent heap corruption. A bare 'fix p all property/atom d_foo' under -k on without -sf kk hits the same path.
suggested_fix: Call AtomKokkos::update_property_atom() (or an equivalent kokkosable check) from AtomKokkos::add_custom(), or have ModifyKokkos force the /kk variant for property/atom regardless of suffix_enable.

summary: ~FixPropertyAtomKokkos() calls atomKK->update_property_atom(), which rebuilds fix_prop_atom[] from modify->get_fix_by_style("^property/atom") while the dying fix is still in Modify's list, leaving a dangling pointer that every later atomKK->sync()/modified() dereferences.
verified_by: orchestrator (Modify::delete_fix src/modify.cpp:1075 deletes the object BEFORE removing it from fix[]/fix_list at :1078-1081; AtomKokkos::update_property_atom src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp:162-174 repopulates from that list).

summary: k_brokenflag is written on the device by the kernel but never marked modified, so k_brokenflag.sync_host() is a no-op on GPU builds and bond quartic/kk never breaks any bond.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_quartic_kokkos.cpp:124 'Kokkos::deep_copy(d_brokenflag,0);' (raw device write, no modify flag), :281 'd_brokenflag(n) = 1;' (device kernel write), :176 'k_brokenflag.sync_host();' with NO preceding 'k_brokenflag.template modify<DeviceType>()' / 'modify_device()'. grep confirms the only k_brokenflag lines in the file are 120,121,122,124,176,182,199,281 - no modify anywhere. Kokkos::DualView::sync_host() only deep-copies when modified_flags(device) > modified_flags(host); both are 0 here, so no D2H copy happens. The host loop then reads h_brokenflag (:182,:199) which stays all-zero. Contrast the correct pattern in the sibling style src/KOKKOS/bond_table_kokkos.cpp:204-205 'k_error_flag.template modify<DeviceType>(); k_error_flag.sync_host();'. CPU base src/MOLECULE/bond_quartic.cpp:102-110 breaks the bond inline (bondlist[n][2]=0 and atom->bond_type[..]=0).
failure_scenario: GPU (CUDA/HIP/SYCL) build, 'bond_style quartic/kk' polymer scission run (e.g. examples/micelle-style FENE/quartic chain scission): a stretched bond with rsq > rc^2 sets d_brokenflag on the device, h_brokenflag stays 0, so h_bondlist(n,2) is never set to 0 and atom->bond_type is never zeroed. No bond is ever broken; the quartic potential silently behaves as an unbreakable bond and the trajectory is wrong. On a CPU-only Kokkos build host and device views alias, so the bug is invisible.
suggested_fix: Add 'k_brokenflag.template modify<DeviceType>();' immediately before the 'k_brokenflag.sync_host();' at line 176 (and mark the deep_copy(d_brokenflag,0) with modify<DeviceType>() as well for consistency).

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly); found by group 03
summary: k_brokenflag is written on the device (deep_copy zero + kernel) but never marked modified, so k_brokenflag.sync_host() is a no-op on GPU builds and the host loop that zeroes broken bonds never sees a set flag: bond quartic/kk never breaks a bond.
evidence: grep k_brokenflag bond_quartic_kokkos.cpp -> lines 120,121,122,176,182 only; no modify<DeviceType>()/modify_device(). Contrast bond_table_kokkos.cpp k_error_flag modify+sync.
failure_scenario: GPU polymer scission run with bond_style quartic/kk: bonds never break; CPU-only Kokkos builds hide it (host and device alias).
suggested_fix: Call k_brokenflag.template modify<DeviceType>() before sync_host().

summary: dihedral_style hybrid/kk keeps the base class default centroidstressflag = CENTROID_AVAIL while every KOKKOS dihedral sub-style sets CENTROID_NOTAVAIL, so with a centroid/stress/atom compute the hybrid enters its cvflag_atom branch and dereferences styles[m]->cvatom, which the sub-styles never allocate (nullptr).
failure_scenario: 'dihedral_style hybrid/kk harmonic opls' plus 'compute p all centroid/stress/atom NULL' and a thermo/dump referencing it: on the first force evaluation cvatom_substyle is nullptr and the inner loop segfaults. Even without the crash the sub-styles' per-atom virial is silently dropped, because the hybrid's own vflag_atom stays 0 while the sub-styles fill vatom.
suggested_fix: Set centroidstressflag = CENTROID_NOTAVAIL in the DihedralHybridKokkos constructor (matching all KOKKOS sub-styles), or make init_style() derive the hybrid's flag from the sub-styles and skip/guard the cvatom accumulation when a sub-style did not produce cvatom. The same shape exists in angle_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:144 and improper_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:146.

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly); found by groups 01/09
summary: dihedral hybrid/kk and improper hybrid/kk (like angle hybrid/kk) never set centroidstressflag, keep CENTROID_AVAIL, and with compute centroid/stress/atom dereference the sub-styles' null cvatom (all kk sub-styles set CENTROID_NOTAVAIL).
evidence: dihedral_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:148-150 and improper_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:149-151 accumulate styles[m]->cvatom; grep centroidstressflag in both files: none.
failure_scenario: *_style hybrid/kk + compute centroid/stress/atom: segfault on the first force evaluation.
suggested_fix: Set centroidstressflag from the sub-styles in the three kk hybrid init_style()s.

summary: pair table/kk stores the special_lj weights into the inherited `int Pair::special_lj[4]`, truncating fractional special-bond factors (0.5 -> 0), so 1-2/1-3/1-4 pair interactions are silently dropped.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_kokkos.cpp:124-127 `special_lj[0] = force->special_lj[0]; ... special_lj[3] = force->special_lj[3];`. PairTableKokkos (src/KOKKOS/pair_table_kokkos.h) declares NO special_lj member and src/pair_table.h has none either, so the name resolves to src/pair.h:247 `int special_lj[4];    // copied from force->special_lj for Kokkos` (force->special_lj is `double[4]`, src/force.h:116). Every other KOKKOS pair style shadows it with its own `KK_FLOAT special_lj[4]` (e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_soft_kokkos.h:89, src/KOKKOS/pair_morse_kokkos.h:90). The functor then reads it: src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:181 `evdwl = factor_lj * c.template compute_evdwl<...>` with `factor_lj = c.special_lj[j >> SBBITS & 3]`.
failure_scenario: `special_bonds lj 0.0 0.0 0.5` + `pair_style table/kk linear N`: force->special_lj[3]=0.5 is stored as int 0, so all 1-4 tabulated pair interactions get factor 0 instead of 0.5 -> wrong forces and energies, silently. The CPU pair_style table gives 0.5. Any non-integer weight (0.5, 0.8333, ...) is affected.
suggested_fix: Declare `KK_FLOAT special_lj[4];` as a member of PairTableKokkos (as every other KOKKOS pair style does), or change src/pair.h:247 to `double special_lj[4];`.

summary: PairTableKokkos::settings() releases the cutsq/tabindex dual views but never frees the aliased legacy row-pointer arrays, leaking them and leaving `cutsq`/`tabindex` dangling and non-null.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_kokkos.cpp:469-477 `if (allocated) { memory->destroy(setflag); d_table_const.tabindex = d_table->tabindex = typename AT::t_int_2d_lr(); h_table->tabindex = HAT::t_int_2d_lr(); d_table_const.cutsq = d_table->cutsq = typename AT::t_double_2d_lr(); h_table->cutsq = HAT::t_double_2d_lr(); }`. The arrays were made by `memoryKK->create_kokkos(d_table->cutsq,h_table->cutsq,cutsq,nt,nt,...)` (line 420), which `smalloc`s an `n1`-entry row-pointer array (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:186-196) that only `destroy_kokkos(TYPE&, value_type**&)` (memory_kokkos.h:297-306) frees and nulls. The CPU base does it properly: src/pair_table.cpp settings() `if (allocated) { memory->destroy(setflag); memory->destroy(cutsq); memory->destroy(tabindex); }`.
failure_scenario: Repeated `pair_style table/kk ...` commands in one input leak the row-pointer arrays each time and leave `cutsq`/`tabindex` pointing at freed view memory; any read of `cutsq[i][j]` before the next `allocate()` is use-after-free.
suggested_fix: Replace the manual view resets with `memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_table->cutsq,cutsq);` and `memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_table->tabindex,tabindex);` (then also reset the host mirrors), matching the destructor at lines 62-63.

summary: Global vdW energy is accumulated under `if (eflag)` rather than `if (eflag_global)`, so eng_vdwl is polluted on steps that request only per-atom energy.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_kokkos.cpp:177 `if (eflag) eng_vdwl += static_cast<double>(ev.evdwl);` while line 178 correctly uses `if (vflag_global)`. src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:180-183 accumulates `ev.evdwl` whenever `c.eflag_either` is set (i.e. also for eflag==2/atom-only), and Pair::ev_setup only zeroes eng_vdwl when eflag_global is set.
failure_scenario: A step where only `compute pe/atom` is invoked (eflag==2, eflag_global==0) adds the full pair energy into eng_vdwl without ever resetting it; any consumer reading Pair::eng_vdwl before the next eflag_global step sees a doubled/stale value.
suggested_fix: Use `if (eflag_global) eng_vdwl += ...` as the other 59 KOKKOS pair styles do.

summary: compute_evdwl for pair_style morse/kk omits the energy offset, so `pair_modify shift yes` has no effect and the pair energy differs from the CPU style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_morse_kokkos.cpp:165-178 reads only r0/d0/alpha and returns `d0 * dexp * ( dexp - static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(2.0) );` - `offset` is never fetched from m_params/params even though it is stored there (src/KOKKOS/pair_morse_kokkos.cpp:238 `k_params.view_host()(i,j).offset = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(offset[i][j]);` and declared at src/KOKKOS/pair_morse_kokkos.h:54). The CPU base src/pair_morse.cpp:119 computes `evdwl = d0[itype][jtype] * (dexp * dexp - 2.0 * dexp) - offset[itype][jtype];`. Sibling KOKKOS styles do subtract it, e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_morse_smooth_linear_kokkos.cpp and src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_smooth_kokkos.cpp:175.
failure_scenario: `pair_style morse 10.0` with `pair_modify shift yes`: pair morse/kk reports an unshifted pair energy (evdwl and per-atom energy differ from pair morse by offset*npairs), while forces are unaffected.
suggested_fix: Fetch `offset` from m_params/params in compute_evdwl and subtract it, mirroring src/pair_morse.cpp:119.

summary: compute_evdwl returns d0*dexp*(dexp-2.0) without subtracting the stored energy offset, so 'pair_modify shift yes' has no effect on morse/kk and both the global and per-atom pair energies differ from the CPU style.
verified_by: orchestrator (src/KOKKOS/pair_morse_kokkos.cpp:165-178 never reads params(...).offset although init_one stores it at :238 and the header declares it at :54; the CPU base subtracts it at src/pair_morse.cpp:119).

summary: The Wolf self-energy is summed on the host from `atom->q[i]` while compute() only syncs q to the device, so on a GPU build the charges are stale after any device-side exchange or atom sort.
failure_scenario: Multi-rank GPU run with `pair_style born/coul/wolf/kk`: after the first atom migration, the host q[0..nlocal) holds the previous step's atoms, so the self-energy in eng_coul is wrong; per-atom energies are wrong even on one rank once atom sorting permutes d_q.
suggested_fix: Move the self-energy into the device kernel using the `q` device view, or sync Q_MASK to the host before the loop and iterate over list->ilist.

summary: The Device branch of AtomVecMolecularKokkos::sync_pinned omits k_dihedral_atom4, so that array is never staged to the device while its dual-view sync flag is cleared by the surrounding transfers.
failure_scenario: Any future/existing caller of atomKK->sync_pinned(Device, DIHEDRAL_MASK) after the host modified the topology (data file read, fix bond/react, molecule template insertion) leaves dihedral_atom4 stale on the device -> the 4th atom of every dihedral is wrong on the GPU.  Currently latent: the three call sites (verlet_kokkos.cpp:448, third_order_kokkos.cpp:230, dynamical_matrix_kokkos.cpp:230) all pass Host/HostKK.
suggested_fix: Add the missing k_dihedral_atom4 need_sync_device()/perform_pinned_copy_transform pair to the Device branch.

summary: kf_bfly_generic() uses the single per-plan scratch view st.d_scratch that every concurrently running 1d FFT of the same parallel_for shares, where the CPU original allocates a private scratch buffer per call.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/kissfft_kokkos.h:387 'typename FFT_AT::t_FFT_DATA_1d_um d_scratch = st.d_scratch;' then :392-393 'd_scratch(q1).re = d_Fout(Fout_count + k).re; ...' and :407 'C_MUL(t,d_scratch,q,d_twiddles,twidx);'. st.d_scratch is allocated once per plan in kiss_fft_alloc_kokkos (src/KOKKOS/kissfft_kokkos.h:520 'st.d_scratch = typename FFT_AT::t_FFT_DATA_1d("kissfft:scratch",p_max);'). The state is copied by value into kiss_fft_functor (src/KOKKOS/fft3d_kokkos.cpp:183-193 'kiss_fft_state_kokkos<DeviceType> st;'), but a Kokkos::View member copies by reference-counted handle, so all threads of 'Kokkos::parallel_for(total/length,f);' (src/KOKKOS/fft3d_kokkos.cpp:261, and the mid/slow equivalents) write the same memory. The CPU original gives every call its own buffer: src/KSPACE/kissfft.h:340 'auto *scratch = (FFT_DATA *) KISS_FFT_TMP_ALLOC(sizeof(FFT_DATA) * p);' ... :362 'KISS_FFT_TMP_FREE(scratch);'.
failure_scenario: Any FFT grid dimension with a prime factor larger than 5 (e.g. nfast = 7) routes kf_work's default switch case to kf_bfly_generic; every one of the total/length concurrent 1d FFTs then reads and writes the same p_max-element scratch view, so the transformed data is garbage (nondeterministic, differs run to run). Today this is latent for PPPM only because PPPM::set_grid_global boosts every grid dimension until PPPM::factorable() accepts it and factors[] is only {2,3,5} (src/KSPACE/pppm.cpp:92-96,1170-1172) -- any future user of FFT3dKokkos with an arbitrary grid size hits it immediately.
suggested_fix: Give each FFT its own scratch slice: size st.d_scratch as p_max*(number of concurrent FFTs) and index it with the functor's 'i' (or the offset/length), or use Kokkos scratch (team) memory instead of a plan-wide view.

summary: FixShardlow, the base class of the Kokkos style that is copied by value into device functors, has no 'if (copymode) return;' guard as the first line of its destructor.
evidence: src/DPD-REACT/fix_shardlow.cpp:118-122 'FixShardlow::~FixShardlow() { memory->destroy(rand_state); maxRNG = 0; }' - no copymode guard ('grep -n copymode src/DPD-REACT/fix_shardlow.cpp' finds nothing).  FixShardlowKokkos passes '*this' to Kokkos::parallel_for at fix_shardlow_kokkos.cpp:624,626,660,662, and its own destructor (fix_shardlow_kokkos.cpp:106-109) also lacks the guard.  .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 1 requires the guard in every base-class destructor a _kokkos style inherits from.
failure_scenario: today only latent: FixShardlowKokkos::initial_integrate overrides the base version, so the private 'rand_state' the base destructor frees is always nullptr and memory->destroy() is a no-op.  Any future code path that lets the base allocate rand_state (or any new allocation added to ~FixShardlow) becomes a double free when the functor copies are destroyed.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (copymode) return;' as the first line of FixShardlow::~FixShardlow() (and of ~FixShardlowKokkos).

summary: FixShardlow::~FixShardlow() lacks the mandatory `if (copymode) return;` guard although FixShardlowKokkos is copied by value into Kokkos functors.
failure_scenario: Today the KOKKOS variant keeps the base `rand_state` pointer at nullptr (it uses the device view d_rand_state, fix_shardlow_kokkos.cpp:592), so memory->destroy() is a no-op and nothing crashes. The moment any code path lets the base allocate rand_state (e.g. a future host fallback calling FixShardlow::initial_integrate, which grows it at fix_shardlow.cpp:532), the functor copy's destructor frees the original's array -> double free / use-after-free in the next `fix shardlow` step with pair dpd/fdt/energy.
suggested_fix: Add `if (copymode) return;` as the first statement of FixShardlow::~FixShardlow().

summary: The class re-declares 'class AtomKokkos *atomKK;' as a private member, shadowing Pointers::atomKK (a reference bound to lmp->atomKK), unlike every other KOKKOS style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_sphere_kokkos.h:81-82 ' private:\n  class AtomKokkos *atomKK;'.  src/pointers.h:131 declares 'class AtomKokkos *&atomKK;' bound to lmp->atomKK (pointers.h:92).  The constructor's 'atomKK = (AtomKokkos *) atom;' (compute_temp_sphere_kokkos.cpp:36) therefore writes the shadowing member instead of lmp->atomKK.  No other file in src/KOKKOS declares an atomKK member (grep 'AtomKokkos \*atomKK' src/KOKKOS/*.h returns only this one).
failure_scenario: Harmless today because atom and lmp->atomKK are the same object, but the member is uninitialized until the derived constructor body runs and any future base-class code path that runs before it (or that reads Pointers::atomKK) sees a different pointer than this class uses.
suggested_fix: Delete the member declaration and use the inherited Pointers::atomKK like the rest of the package.

summary: In non-GPU-aware mode remap_3d_kokkos() re-creates the host mirrors of the scratch and send buffers with Kokkos::create_mirror_view() on every call, i.e. a fresh host allocation of the full scratch size for each of the several remaps per FFT per timestep.
evidence: remap_kokkos.cpp:123-128: 'if (!plan->usegpu_aware) { plan->h_scratch = Kokkos::create_mirror_view(d_scratch); plan->h_sendbuf = Kokkos::create_mirror_view(plan->d_sendbuf); ... }' executed unconditionally at the top of every remap_3d_kokkos() call; on a GPU backend create_mirror_view allocates (d_scratch is not host accessible). The plan struct keeps h_scratch/h_sendbuf as members, so they could be allocated once (or resized when the extents change).
failure_scenario: PPPM/kk on a GPU without GPU-aware MPI: each timestep performs 4 remaps per 3d FFT (2-3 FFTs), each allocating and freeing a host buffer of nqty*out.isize*out.jsize*out.ksize FFT_SCALARs; pure overhead, no wrong results.
suggested_fix: Allocate h_scratch/h_sendbuf once in remap_3d_create_plan_kokkos (or lazily when their extent differs from the device view), not on every call.

summary: improper umbrella/kk allocates a brand-new Kokkos DualView for the warning flag on every timestep inside compute() instead of once in the constructor.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/improper_umbrella_kokkos.cpp:97-103 inside compute(): `// zero warning flag` / `k_warning_flag = DAT::tdual_int_scalar("ImproperUmbrella::warning_flag");` / `d_warning_flag = k_warning_flag.template view<DeviceType>();` ... Every other KOKKOS bonded style creates it once in the constructor, e.g. src/KOKKOS/improper_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:46-48 (in the ctor) and then only does `h_warning_flag() = 0; k_warning_flag.modify_host(); k_warning_flag.sync<DeviceType>();` per step (improper_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:102-104). improper_fourier_kokkos.cpp:99-101 has the same per-step allocation.
failure_scenario: Every MD step with improper_style umbrella/kk performs a device allocation+free (cudaMalloc/cudaFree class of call), which serializes the GPU stream; measurable overhead in improper-dominated runs. No wrong numbers.
suggested_fix: Move the `k_warning_flag = DAT::tdual_int_scalar(...)` / `d_warning_flag` / `h_warning_flag` initialization into the constructor as improper_harmonic_kokkos does, keeping only the zeroing in compute().

summary: Error message names the wrong pair style ("pair tersoff/kk") in the tersoff/mod/c/kk (and mod, zbl) variants.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_mod_c_kokkos.cpp:120-121 `if (neighflag == FULL) error->all(FLERR,"Must use half neighbor list style with pair tersoff/kk");` - identical copy-pasted text in pair_tersoff_mod_kokkos.cpp:121 and pair_tersoff_zbl_kokkos.cpp:134.
failure_scenario: A user running `pair_style tersoff/mod/c/kk` with `package kokkos neigh full` is told to fix `pair tersoff/kk`, a style that is not in their input.
suggested_fix: Use the real style name in each variant's message (tersoff/mod/c/kk, tersoff/mod/kk, tersoff/zbl/kk).
